slides.1.title: Question 1: why high-acid base wine?
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The logic of cool climates
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Sparkling wine needs high-acid, low-alcohol, neutral base wine: the second fermentation adds more alcohol, and acidity carries the freshness of the bubbles. Hence top regions tend to be cool or marginal
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Approaches in warm regions
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Warm regions keep acidity through early picking, altitude or cool coastal sites, a challenge every region now shares as the climate warms
slides.1.content: Quality sparkling wine starts with a high-acid base wine that is not pleasant on its own.
slides.2.title: Question 2: where does the second fermentation happen?
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Traditional method
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Second fermentation, lees ageing, riddling and disgorgement all in the same bottle; the most expensive, giving fine bubbles and autolytic character
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Transfer method
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Second fermentation and ageing in bottle, then emptied into a pressurised tank, filtered and rebottled, skipping riddling
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Tank method
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Second fermentation in a sealed tank, then filtration and bottling; quick and cheap, preserving primary fruit
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Ancestral method
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Bottled before the first fermentation finishes, which then completes in bottle: a single fermentation
slides.2.content: Methods are not better or worse: they are choices of style goal and cost.

slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Why are top sparkling-wine regions usually cool?
A. They need high-acid, low-alcohol base wine
B. Cool regions pay less tax
C. MLF only works in the cool
D. Cool regions need no yeast
The second fermentation adds more alcohol.
Which method costs the most and gives autolytic character?
Lees ageing ties up time and capital.
What is the main style advantage of the tank method?
A. It gives the highest alcohol
B. It requires long bottle ageing
C. It preserves fresh primary fruit
D. It gives the strongest autolytic character
Quick and cheap, and suited to young drinking.
